raw_response.country: Canada (with brief comparative discussion of the United States, Australia, Greenland/Denmark, Finland, Norway and Sweden)

criterion_notes.c1: Addresses household and community water insecurity, drinking water systems (piped supply, trucked water, wells and household cisterns) and drinking water advisories restricting consumption or use on Indigenous reserves in Canada.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (c2 = no): the authors explicitly restrict the review's scope to technical and microbiological issues, mentioning shared federal/First Nations administration, funding delays and provincial/federal drinking-water quality guidelines or advisory classifications only as brief unanalysed macro-governance and regulatory background rather than analysing a rule-type mechanism governing service access. Under the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2, the descriptive background on fragmented federal-provincial-First Nations governance and water-advisory issuance is at most tangential context rather than a studied factor, and plain_criterion2_decision remains 'exclude' because the paper also lacks empirical governance-access evidence or a systematic empirical synthesis (c3 = no).
criterion_notes.c3: Narrative 'multifaceted review' summarizing 169 articles and 18 government portals without systematic-review methodology (no formal eligibility criteria, study selection protocol, quality appraisal or structured synthesis). The Data Availability Statement explicitly notes 'This is a literature review' (a brief parenthetical citation to unpublished microbial colony counts from one Manitoba community includes no study methods and examines water-quality microbiology rather than access governance).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports secondary descriptive statistics from government portals on short-term and long-term drinking water advisories (boiling water, do not consume and do not use advisories) and lack of piped water/basic sanitation in Indigenous communities, although most of the review focuses on microbial/chemical water quality and diagnostic technologies.
criterion_notes.c5: As a non-systematic narrative review focused on microbiology, natural organic matter removal and molecular monitoring tools, it lacks an identifiable empirical study design linking a defined unit-of-analysis sample, a legal/administrative exposure and a service-access outcome.

evidence_quotes.quote: Water advisories are issued by local authorities to communities to warn about water consumption or completely restrict its usage. It is estimated that in Canada there are more than 100 short-term drinking water advisories at any given time (Indigenous Services Canada, 2024a). As of September 2024, there are more than 30 long-term drinking water advisories remaining in Indigenous reserves (Indigenous Services Canada, 2024a).

While we restricted the scope of this review to technical and microbiological issues, we acknowledge that water insecurity is the result of socio-cultural, systemic disparities, historic and institutionalized marginalization of Indigenous people, and an ineffective and segregated system of water governance that applies to FN reserves (Meehan et al., 2020).

evidence_quotes.page: PMC PMC11493031 - Water advisories in Canada
evidence_quotes.quote: Additionally, in Indigenous reserves, water delivery, and maintenance responsibilities are shared between the Federal Government, specifically Indigenous Services Canada and Health Canada with FN community leadership groups (Boyd, 2011; Bradford et al., 2016; Lucier et al., 2020). This shared administration and fragmented responsibilities has led to divergences in drinking water regulations in Indigenous reserves (Boyd, 2011; Bradford et al., 2016).

This investigation synthesizes existing literature and Canadian public records concerning the prolonged state of water insecurity in Indigenous reserves to promote comprehension of the microbiological and chemical risks that this represents for public health.

Peer-reviewed publications, theses, and government portals addressing the following topics were retained for the final report: Water insecurity in Indigenous communities in Canada, DWS in Indigenous communities, Drinking water treatments, NOM, water storage tanks in Indigenous communities in Canada, microorganisms, metagenomics for water monitoring, culturomics, and microfluidics.

raw_response.outcome: Secondary government counts of short-term and long-term drinking water advisories and descriptive summaries of microbial/chemical water quality and water treatment/monitoring methods
raw_response.population_and_sample: Indigenous reserves / First Nations communities in Canada (narrative review citing 169 articles and 18 government portals; no primary empirical sample)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). The article is a non-systematic narrative 'multifaceted review' ('This is a literature review') synthesizing secondary literature and government portals on microbial risks in water storage tanks, natural organic matter (NOM), drinking water treatment processes and molecular microbial monitoring tools (metagenomics, culturomics and microfluidics). In addition to lacking primary empirical governance-access analysis or systematic-review methodology (c3 = no, c5 = no), the authors explicitly restrict their scope to technical and microbiological issues, treating shared federal/First Nations governance and regulatory fragmentation only as unanalysed background (c2 = no under narrow rule-type scope; plain_criterion2_decision is also exclude).
raw_response.study_design: Narrative literature review (multifaceted review of secondary literature and government portals)
